hypotheses.reconstruction_rule: Each member A_i is recovered by applying the divided-difference operator specified in its operator args to the latent function F(z)=s(z). G0001 uses Newton divided difference nodes [p,q]; G0002 uses Hermite divided difference with repeated node [p,p], which gives the derivative ds(p); G0003 uses Hermite divided difference nodes [p,p,q].
required_assumptions: p and q are distinct where division by p-q occurs
s is differentiable at p and ds(p) is the derivative of s at p
Hermite divided differences with repeated nodes are interpreted as derivative limits
hypotheses.scientific_rationale: The three non-identical catalog members are divided-difference evaluations of the same latent univariate function s(z). G0001 is the first divided difference s[p,q]; G0002 is the repeated-node Hermite divided difference s[p,p] expressed as the derivative ds(p); G0003 is the mixed second Hermite divided difference s[p,p,q]. This representation explains all three members via one latent object and explicit divided-difference operators without claiming an algebraic simplification.
